findings.description: values.sort() with no comparator sorts lexicographically, so numbers are ordered as strings and the median is wrong. It also sorts the caller's array in place, mutating input.
findings.scenario: median([10, 9, 2, 1, 100]) sorts to [1, 10, 100, 2, 9] and returns 100 instead of 9; the caller's array is also reordered.

findings.description: median on an empty array computes (undefined + undefined) / 2 and returns NaN. The file's own comment says empty arrays are legitimate.
findings.fix: if (sorted.length === 0) return null; (or throw a clear error) before computing mid.

findings.description: percentile on an empty array gives idx = Math.min(-1, 0) = -1 and returns sorted[-1], i.e. undefined, silently. p is also not validated, so p > 100 or p < 0 gives clamped or undefined results.
findings.scenario: percentile([], 50) returns undefined; percentile([1,2,3], -10) gives idx -1 and returns undefined.
findings.fix: if (!values.length) return null; and clamp the index: Math.max(0, Math.min(sorted.length - 1, ...)).

findings.description: average divides by values.length with no empty check. The comment above states new users have empty data, so this is a reachable case that returns NaN, which will show up in the dashboard.
findings.scenario: average([]) is 0 / 0 = NaN for a new user.
findings.fix: if (values.length === 0) return 0; (or null, whichever the dashboard expects) before the reduce.

findings.description: The loop uses var i, so every setTimeout callback shares one i. When the callbacks fire, i equals jobs.length and jobs[i] is undefined. Every job runs with undefined and none of the real jobs run.
findings.scenario: scheduleJobs([a, b, c], run) calls run(undefined) three times.
findings.fix: Use let: for (let i = 0; i < jobs.length; i++) { setTimeout(() => run(jobs[i]), i * 100); }

findings.description: managerName guards user.manager but not user itself. user.manager.name may also be undefined for a manager object without a name, returning undefined instead of a string.
findings.scenario: managerName(null) throws TypeError; managerName({manager:{}}) returns undefined.
